messages.text: wait, did you actually push the token bucket code? i see a new commit on the branch but it looks like you just hardcoded the limit to 1000 req/min. that's basically nothing for a pdf import.
it's a placeholder. i know. 1000 is fine for our internal testing but yeah, we need tighter limits before anyone external touches it. the real config comes from env vars in the hardening pass.
ok. also, are we setting the body size limit? i see nginx is set to 16m but express default is 100kb. if someone uploads a legit linkedin export it might fail silently.
good catch. i'll bump the json body limit to 12mb in the middleware. that should cover most resumes and profile dumps without eating all the memory.
also, health checks. are we returning a 200 on /health if the db is down? i just curled it and got a 200 even though i stopped postgres locally.
yeah, that's bad. it should check the connection pool. i'll add a quick pg query to the health endpoint so it actually fails if we're disconnected.
can you add that to the checklist in docs/decisions.md? i want to make sure we don't forget it when we do the final sweep before the freeze.
done. added: 'health check validates db connection' under the hardening section. also noting that we need to log request ids for the import endpoint so we can trace spam attempts later.
we should have a staging env for this. i don't want to be testing auth flows on prod while you're still tweaking the token bucket logic.
there's no time for a full staging setup before the freeze. we have 4 days. i'd rather spend that time fixing the actual bugs than spinning up a new docker compose env.
fair. but let's at least use a separate database schema for your local testing. don't want you wiping out the seeded concept graph again.
i already am using a throwaway container. just be careful with the shared volume mounts when you're doing your docker stuff tomorrow.
